description: The bar chart on the left illustrates the relationship between Ambiguity Standard and Fleiss Kappa, a statistical measure of inter-rater agreement for categorical items. The horizontal axis represents Ambiguity Standard, with values 0.0, 0.47, 0.82, and 0.94. The vertical axis is labeled Fleiss Kappa, with values ranging from 0.0 to 0.8. The chart shows four bars, each corresponding to a different Ambiguity Standard value. The bar at 0.0 has the highest Fleiss Kappa value of 0.88, indicating the highest agreement among raters. The bar at 0.47 has a Fleiss Kappa value of 0.46, and the bar at 0.82 has a value of 0.03, which is the lowest, suggesting the least agreement. The bar at 0.94 has a Fleiss Kappa value of 0.24, indicating a moderate level of agreement. The chart on the right displays the relationship between Max Ambiguity and Fleiss Kappa. The horizontal axis is labeled Max Ambiguity with values 1, 2, and 3. The vertical axis is the same as the left chart, Fleiss Kappa. The bar at 1 has the highest Fleiss Kappa value of 0.89, while the bar at 2 has a value of 0.46, and the bar at 3 has a value of 0.23, indicating a decrease in agreement as the Max Ambiguity increases. Both charts use a single color for the bars, and there are no additional visual elements such as shading or annotations.
